description: Its mane is a crown of ice that never melts. The cold arrives a breath before it does, and stays after.
lore: You get the number before you get the animal: the fire wants twice the wood. Then it is at the rim of the light, heavy through the shoulders, a crest of ice grown up out of its neck like a crown hammered on wrong, icicles off the jaw, ice standing out through the claws. It does not come in. It has never once come in.

[[characters/cfe826c1|Jehanne]] had one at her fire for six hours in the black of a winter, with four people to keep warm and the pile going down and the tellings stopped, because you cannot tell a thing properly while you are hauling. A man there wanted it driven off and was right on every practical count. She fed the fire and let it stand, and said afterwards only that a rota does not get to ask who is coming. What she keeps to herself, because it does her no credit as a keeper, is why she thinks it stands there: it is trying to get warm. The cold is the last true thing it has left, and it puts out whatever it walks toward, and cannot learn this, and comes back. She splits a second pile now on the nights the frost arrives early. The man still keeps the rota with her. They have not discussed it once.
gm_notes: Shipped description adopted verbatim — 'the cold arrives a breath before it does' is exactly the art and exactly the mechanic. Sad-before-evil: it is not besieging the fire, it is queueing at it. Jehanne's beat is practice outrunning belief, in the smallest possible form — an extra woodpile. Never let it enter the ring of light; the record dies the moment it does. No stone or leavings bound yet.
